text:
Alex: Quick update — ran a short bring-up for stratus-11b (int6) against our current 13b fp16 baseline on customer slice A. TL;DR and recs below.

Maria: nice, hit me with the numbers. :eyes:

Alex: Results (2k sample, mixed-turn chat + rerank subset):
- Cost: int6 ~= $0.28 / 1k tokens, 13b fp16 ~= $0.41 / 1k tokens (approx, infra blended).
- Latency: int6 p50 55ms, p95 140ms; 13b fp16 p50 70ms, p95 190ms.
- Quality (primary score = exact-answer F1): int6 -0.9pp vs 13b on dialogue QA, rerank NDCG drop 0.7pp.
- Failure modes: hallucination rate up on very long-context prompts (>1k tokens), some tokenization edge cases in priming.

Derek: those p95 wins are nice. the quality delta looks small but not negligible. any slice breakdown?

Alex: slice breakdown: short queries (<256 tokens) — int6 parity or slight win on latency; long-form answers (>512 tokens) — quality gap widens, esp. multi-step reasoning prompts. Rerank slice: int6 is acceptable for cost-sensitive endpoints.

Priya: product note — which endpoints could we default to int6 safely for GTN?

Alex: proposal:
1) Default int6 for: conversational read-only endpoints, embeddings generation, and baseline rerank flows.
2) Keep 13b fp16 for: codegen, multi-step reasoning, and official docs/compose endpoints.
3) Hybrid routing rule: if prompt.length > 512 OR complexity_score >= 0.6 -> route to 13b; else route to int6.

Maria: +1. what's the rollout plan? canary sizes, metrics to watch?

Alex: rollout suggestion: 5% traffic for 48h, expand to 20% if:
- no regression > 1.0pp in exact-answer F1 on canary slice
- latency p95 stays below SLO + 50ms
- error rate stable (<0.1% increase)

Derek: add tracing tag so we can correlate prompt types with regressions. also surface top-k examples where int6 disagreed.

Alex: yep, capturing disagreement diffs and saving top 50 counterexamples to s3: s3://redwood-eval/stratus-int6/counterexamples/1767778888/
Command I ran:```bash
./run_eval --model stratus-11b-int6 --baseline 13b-fp16 --slice customerA --samples 2000 --save-disagreements
```

EvalBot: regression-checker: alert=FALSE; observed quality delta -0.9pp (below 1.0pp threshold) but margin close. Recommend manual review of top disagreements.

Priya: For GTN messaging: frame as "~30% unit-cost reduction for quick-response flows with similar UX; we recommend phased rollout with product flags." Keep a note that long-form editors remain on 13b.

Maria: any ops flags required? autoscaler, kv-cache changes?

Alex: ops notes:
- kv-cache logic unchanged.
- autoscaler suggested target add: reduce min replicas for int6 pool by 1 to save standing cost, monitor latency.
- quantized model needs periodic warmup on new pods to avoid cold-kv latency spike — add warmup hook in deploy script.

Derek: can we make fallback fast if a regression is detected? like immediate 100% fallback for flagged customers?

Alex: yes — we already have route policy that can fall back by customer id; will add a temp flag with TTL. plan: canary 5% -> auto rollback if regression triggers >1pp on monitored metric.

Priya: For GTN, I'll draft a short blurb and a playbook: recommended endpoints, expected savings, and escalation steps. Tagging growth/product for approval. @Maria @Alex please add the final numbers to the playbook.

Alex: will open PR with routing rule and canary config, and create a short spreadsheet with detailed per-slice deltas. linking PR when ready. :rocket:

Maria: ack. please ping on the canary start.

EvalBot: note: scheduled follow-up perf run in 24h to collect more tail samples.

Alex: thanks all — keeping this conservative. any last thoughts?

Priya: none from me. sounds good.

Derek: :thumbsup:
